title: 20-50 Occupancy Test
rule: At least 20% of residential units must be occupied by individuals or families whose income is at or below 50% of the Area Median Gross Income (AMGI).

title: 40-60 Occupancy Test
rule: At least 40% of residential units must be occupied by individuals or families whose income is at or below 60% of the Area Median Gross Income (AMGI).

title: Qualified Project Period
rule: A project must satisfy the selected occupancy test throughout the qualified project period.

title: Annual Income Verification
rule: Tenant income must be determined at least annually.

title: Existing Tenant Income Increase
rule: A tenant who initially qualified remains qualified unless income exceeds 140% of the applicable income limit and the next available comparable unit is rented to an over-income tenant.

title: Deep Rent Skewed Threshold
rule: For deep rent skewed projects, the threshold increases from 140% to 170% of the applicable income limit.

title: Deep Rent Skewed Requirement
rule: At least 15% of low-income units must be occupied by households earning 40% or less of the Area Median Gross Income.

title: Deep Rent Gross Rent Limit
rule: Gross rent for each low-income unit must not exceed 30% of the applicable income limit.

title: Comparable Rent Rule
rule: Gross rent for each low-income unit must not exceed one-half of the average gross rent of comparable unrestricted units.

title: Annual Project Certification
rule: Project operators must submit an annual certification confirming continued compliance.

title: Rent Restricted Unit
rule: Gross rent must not exceed 30% of the applicable imputed income limitation.

title: Income Increase Treatment
rule: A unit remains a low-income unit if occupants originally qualified and the unit continues to be rent restricted.

title: Next Available Unit Rule
rule: If tenant income exceeds 140% of the limit, the next available comparable unit must be rented to a qualifying low-income household.

title: Building Qualification Deadline
rule: A project must satisfy the low-income housing requirements by the end of the first year of the credit period.

title: Scattered Site Projects
rule: Buildings may be treated as a single project if all dwelling units are rent-restricted.

title: Annual Recertification Waiver
rule: The Secretary may waive annual tenant income recertification if the entire building is occupied by low-income tenants.

title: MTSP Income Limit Hold Harmless
rule: For non-impacted MTSPs, the income limit may never decline and is the highest value reached during the project's qualifying period.

title: MTSP 60% Income Limit
rule: The MTSP 60% income limit is calculated as 1.2 times the MTSP Very Low-Income Limit (VLIL).

title: Impacted Project VLIL
rule: For HUD impacted projects, VLIL equals the greater of the previous impacted VLIL or the FY2008 VLIL adjusted by median family income growth.

title: Hold Harmless After 2008
rule: Area Median Gross Income for MTSP projects after 2008 may not be lower than the previous year's determination.

title: Four-Person Income Limit
rule: HUD initially sets the four-person very low-income limit at 50% of Area Median Family Income before applying statutory adjustments.

title: High Housing Cost Adjustment
rule: HUD increases very low-income limits when rental housing costs are unusually high relative to median family income.

title: High Income Area Adjustment
rule: HUD reduces very low-income limits in unusually high-income areas subject to statutory minimums.

title: Nonmetropolitan Minimum
rule: Income limits may not be lower than the state's nonmetropolitan median family income level.

title: Annual Increase Cap
rule: For FY2026, annual income limit increases are capped at 10%.
